reason: The same finding as the one below, seen from the other end. This query is not about a step that writes a cache; it is about a step that executes code from an untrusted checkout, because code running on the runner can read the cache token and poison entries whatever the step was nominally doing. Setting enable-cache: false on setup-uv did remove a cache write the release job never needed, and it is kept for that reason, but the alert simply moved to the first step that runs the checked-out tree, which is `make verify`. Any release workflow that builds the commit it is releasing has such a step, so there is no version of this job that does not carry this finding. What bounds it is the same thing that bounds the checkout: `authorize` proves the commit is a signed annotated tag object on main before this job starts.

The release build checks out the commit `authorize` resolved from the tag input, which is the shape this query looks for. `authorize` first proves the tag is an annotated tag object, that its signature verifies against the committed allowed-signers list, and that its commit is an ancestor of main; dispatch additionally requires write access to this repository. The query cannot see a prior job's runtime checks, so it reports what it can see. Excluding the rule outright would switch it off for an unverified checkout added later, and rewriting the checkout as a shell git command would hide the pattern without changing what runs. Kept, and re-read whenever release.yml changes.
